title: Machine learning optimizes micropropagation of Scoparia dulcis
summary: Leaf explants were cultured on MS medium with plant growth regulators: MS + BAP 1 mg/L + NAA 0.5 mg/L gave up to 10.33 ± 1.28 shoots per explant and half-strength MS + IAA 1.5 mg/L gave 6.93 ± 0.61 roots. Random Forest was the best model for shoot number and Gaussian Process Regression for root number. In the reviewed material the RF-predicted optimum of 10.15 shoots was confirmed at 11.8 ± 0.92 and the GPR-predicted 7.76 roots at 7.26 ± 0.35, with ML optima beating conventional conditions in 2 of 3 shoot and 3 of 3 root parameters. Data come from a single species and a small experimental dataset.
ai_technology: Random Forest and Gaussian Process Regression trained on tissue-culture data

evidence.tested: Wet-lab confirmation of model-predicted hormone optima.
evidence.unknown: Generality beyond this species and dataset; full text not reviewed.
